scores.tell: Cauldron on a pale lilac floor with a pink striped back wall. The floor and wall are plain, but the room corner is a bit more of a set than the real ledge cards. The ember glow under the cauldron is an invented prop.

Full city skyline, glass railing, potted plant and bench, all in soft focus. This is much busier than real category 4 cards. The binocular has a face-like look (invented whimsy). The small bench and plant crowd the edges.

Park scene with two trees, hedges, a path, a skyline, flowers and grass tufts. The detail is dense and spread across the whole card, so it competes with the hero. The real swing card has fewer, larger shapes. The table and stools are still central.
Flat pink wall above a purple ledge. This is a clean category 2 setup like the real cards. The only tell is that the pink and purple split is very plain.
Tone-on-tone diamond pattern with a plain orange ground. The backdrop is quiet and the hero is not crowded. The diamonds are a little high-contrast.

The door is wrapped in ivy, with a flower wreath, a bow, cracked plaster and paving. That is a lot of secondary props and small leaves around the edges. It reads as a scene, not a quiet environment. It is busier than any real card.
Blue radial rays with tone-on-tone music notes and stars. This matches the real whistle pattern backdrop, and the pattern is quiet. The stars and notes are slightly large.

Beach with sea, clouds, sand, a cow-face logo and ice cubes. The backdrop is a real environment with many parts, and the cow face is invented whimsy. The sky, sea and sand bands are busy but readable.
Stage podium, spotlight beam, radial rays and glow. The staging is theatrical, and the many stacked effects compete with the busy drum kit. This is more than a flat field or a plain ledge.
Page unavailable: no image was returned for this card, so I could not judge it. The score is a placeholder.
